verdicts.title: Exact Ramsey Theory: Green-Tao numbers and SAT
verdicts.abstract_excerpt: We consider the links between Ramsey theory in the integers, based on van der Waerden's theorem, and (boolean, CNF) SAT solving. We aim at using the problems from exact Ramsey theory, concerned with computing Ramsey-type numbers, as a rich source of test problems, where especially methods for solving hard problems can be developed. In order to control the growth of the problem instances, we introduce "transversal extensions" as a natural way of constructing mixed parameter tuples (k_1, ..., k_m)
verdicts.judge_reasoning: The abstract discusses Ramsey theory, Green-Tao numbers, and SAT solver benchmarking ('rich source of test problems'), with no mention of affine schemes, local induction dimension, or any algebraic-geometric complexity correspondence with SAT.

verdicts.title: Local Backbones
verdicts.abstract_excerpt: A backbone of a propositional CNF formula is a variable whose truth value is the same in every truth assignment that satisfies the formula. The notion of backbones for CNF formulas has been studied in various contexts. In this paper, we introduce local variants of backbones, and study the computational complexity of detecting them. verdicts.title: GraphSAT -- a decision problem connecting satisfiability and graph theory
